descriptors.descriptor_text: Continuous proton-transport pathway with no disruptive phase transition across the cold-to-room operating window (~182–299 K), i.e., no freezing/crystallisation/eutectic segregation that breaks percolation at sub-zero temperatures.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Maintains a single connected confined hydrogen-bond network so VTF-like, relaxation-controlled transport remains valid over the full measurement span.
required_material_features: Single-phase (or percolated two-phase) morphology maintained from ~182 K to ~299 K
Suppressed crystallisation/freezing of the conducting fraction under confinement
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: Confined acid-water network with VTF-governed hybrid hopping; continuity requirement implied by VTF-governed transport

descriptors.descriptor_text: Bound-water/plasticiser continuity down to ~200 K: the conducting fraction must retain a mobile, hydrogen-bonded polar fluid (bound water and/or anti-freeze co-solvent) so proton hopping is not quenched by rigidification.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Provides the dynamically relaxing polar medium whose structural relaxation rate governs proton mobility (VTF behavior).
required_material_features: High fraction of non-freezing (strongly bound/confined) water or equivalent polar plasticiser
Hydrogen-bond network remains labile below 253 K
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: VTF-governed hybrid hopping in confined hydrated acid network

descriptors.descriptor_text: Matrix flexibility below 253 K: the host scaffold must avoid a glassy-brittle state that disconnects channels; it should preserve segmental freedom or an amorphous interfacial layer enabling relaxation-coupled transport at low temperature.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Prevents mechanical/segmental arrest from throttling the relaxation-controlled conductivity and breaking nanoscale connectivity.
required_material_features: Host has sufficiently low effective Tg in the hydrated/plasticised state
No brittle microcracking or pore collapse upon cooling
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: Relaxation-controlled (VTF) transport coupled to host/plasticiser dynamics

descriptors.descriptor_text: Cold-stable acid form within confinement: the proton source must remain in a mobile, non-crystallising speciation under 182–299 K conditions (e.g., buffered/partially neutralised/complexed acid species rather than a neat crystallising acid phase).
descriptors.mechanism_role: Ensures the proton-donor reservoir stays liquid-like and participates in the hydrogen-bond network rather than precipitating into an insulating solid phase.
required_material_features: Acid speciation that resists crystallisation/phase separation under cooling
Sustained ionic dissociation (available mobile protons) at low temperature
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: Confined hydrated-acid network must remain mobile; avoids acid crystallisation-driven loss of conduction

descriptors.descriptor_text: Interconnected nanoconfinement of the conducting fraction: the architecture must confine the hydrated acid network in nanometric domains while still providing a percolated pathway (no isolated pools), to couple mobility to structural relaxation and suppress bulk-like freezing.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Creates the confined acid–water network responsible for hybrid hopping and VTF-type temperature dependence.
required_material_features: Nanometer-scale channels/pores or interfacial layers that host the polar conducting phase
Percolation of these domains across the membrane thickness

descriptors.descriptor_text: Dense hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor landscape enabling hybrid (vehicular + Grotthuss-like) proton transfer: the conducting phase must provide contiguous proton relay sites with short hopping distances and high hydrogen-bond connectivity.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Enables fast proton translocation within the confined network, with transport rate governed by network relaxation (VTF).
required_material_features: High concentration of protonatable sites and hydrogen-bond acceptors in the conducting phase
Continuous hydrogen-bond connectivity (no long nonpolar gaps)
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: Hybrid hopping within confined hydrogen-bond network

descriptors.descriptor_text: Strong retention of the conducting phase without over-binding protons: the host must immobilise/retain acid and water (low leaching/volatility) while avoiding excessive ion-pairing or proton trapping that would reduce effective proton mobility.
descriptors.mechanism_role: Stabilises composition and maintains a high population of mobile charge carriers consistent with observed conductivity trends.
required_material_features: Specific interactions that confine/retain the polar phase under thermal cycling
Moderate binding strength that preserves high proton activity and minimizes fixed ion pairing
descriptors.derived_from_mechanism: Compositionally stable confined acid–water network required for reproducible VTF behavior

extraction_notes: Descriptors are framed to enforce sub-zero (182–299 K) operability consistent with a relaxation-controlled, confined hydrated-acid proton network (VTF), emphasizing suppression of freezing/crystallisation and preservation of a percolated, dynamically mobile hydrogen-bonded phase.
